findings.summary: Apparent inconsistency between T3.3 (MCP init reverted) and T4.3 (MCP init accepted) is substantively justified, not a real inconsistency
findings.rationale: ADR-0040 names exactly five agents that get `mcp__serena__*` plus, for review-architecture-auditor, `mcp__gitnexus__*`: review-architecture-auditor, design-cc (design-claude-code), design-cicd, design-codespaces, discovery-codebase-researcher. Three of those five (design-claude-code, design-cicd, design-codespaces) ALREADY carry the identical `## MCP initialization (REQUIRED)` section verbatim — committed in 6f46d14 (devcontainer-mcp-provisioning-r1 Phases 0-4). The section is therefore the established project-wide MCP init discipline for Serena+GitNexus-consuming agents, not a per-task ornament. review-architecture-auditor is the FOURTH such agent and it consumes BOTH MCPs (Serena + GitNexus), making the init section more load-bearing here than in any of the existing three. T4.3's quality handler reached the substantively correct decision. The apparent inconsistency with T3.3 evaporates once the discipline is recognized: discovery-codebase-researcher (the fifth agent) is the OUTLIER that still lacks the init section — T3.3 cycle-1 reverted it because it was out-of-scope FOR THAT TASK, not because the content was wrong. The reversion was a scope-discipline decision, not a content-discipline decision.

cross_task_consistency_decision.issue: T4.3 added `## MCP initialization (REQUIRED)` to review-architecture-auditor.md; T3.3 reverted the same addition from discovery-codebase-researcher.md
cross_task_consistency_decision.option_selected: Option 3 — defer to broader principle determination; the addition in T4.3 is substantively defensible
cross_task_consistency_decision.reasoning: Investigation revealed: (a) three of the five ADR-0040-named MCP-consumer agents (design-claude-code, design-cicd, design-codespaces) already carry the identical section, committed pre-T4.3 in 6f46d14; (b) review-architecture-auditor is the only agent in the project that consumes BOTH `mcp__serena__*` AND `mcp__gitnexus__*` (per its tools allowlist and ADR-0040's blast-radius-analysis rationale), making the init discipline strictly MORE load-bearing here than in the three design agents that already carry it; (c) T3.3's reversion was a SCOPE-DISCIPLINE decision (the section was outside T3.3's declared FR-9 Blocks-X scope on discovery-codebase-researcher.md), NOT a CONTENT-DISCIPLINE decision; (d) T4.3's declared scope on review-architecture-auditor.md included the Phase 6 design-realization audit, which directly invokes both `mcp__gitnexus__*` (blast-radius) and Bash subprocess on `auditing-shared/scripts/`, meaning the MCP init preconditions are causally necessary for the in-scope content to function correctly. The T4.3 handler's lenient interpretation is the substantively correct one because the MCP init is a precondition for the in-scope Phase 6 work it added; the T3.3 handler's strict interpretation was also correct because T3.3's in-scope FR-9 work did NOT depend on Serena/GitNexus init.
cross_task_consistency_decision.consistency_principle_applied: Scope-deviation is judged by whether the additive content is (a) declared in task scope OR (b) a causal precondition for declared-in-scope content. T4.3 satisfies (b); T3.3 satisfied neither. Different verdicts are therefore consistent under a principled rule, not contradictory.
cross_task_consistency_decision.outcome: Keep the MCP init section in review-architecture-auditor.md. Do not dispatch reconciliation. Phase 4 PASS.
cross_task_consistency_decision.follow_up_oi: I-PQ-P4-002 — add the section to discovery-codebase-researcher.md in a future feature run for project-wide uniformity across the five ADR-0040-named MCP-consumer agents.
